samples.summary: The gutter's defence-in-depth sanitization of self-reported author names is untested — removing the call would break no test
samples.evidence: `authorOfRange` calls `sanitizeDisplayName(best.author)` and the surrounding comment argues this boundary sanitization is essential because no store is trusted. But no test in `blame-gutter.test.ts` ever passes a name that needs sanitizing: every `span(...)` author is 'ann'/'bob'/''/null. The one test that could look like coverage — 'falls back to Anonymous when the author has no name' (blame-gutter.test.ts:75) — passes `''`, which yields `ANONYMOUS_AUTHOR` with or without the sanitize call, so it is vacuous with respect to sanitization. `display-name.test.ts` tests the function in isolation and `remote-selection.test.ts:53` tests the caret path, but nothing asserts the gutter/label path strips `‮`, zero-widths or over-length names, nor that the rendered gutter DOM contains none of them.

samples.summary: No test asserts the blame gutter renders to the LEFT of the line numbers, the feature's headline acceptance criterion and its most fragile constraint
samples.evidence: blame-gutter.ts:12-14 and editor.ts:351-353 depend on `noteBlameGutter` being listed before `basicSetup` in facet order; the todo doc (docs/tasks/active/20260822-notes-blame-gutter-todo.md:9) states 'A blame gutter sits left of the line numbers' as an acceptance criterion. Every DOM assertion in the tests goes through `gutterLabels()`/`querySelector('.cm-noteBlame')`, which are order-agnostic: reordering the extension so the gutter renders right of `.cm-lineNumbers` keeps all tests green. No grep hit for `cm-lineNumbers` anywhere in packages/notes/src tests.

samples.summary: The React glue that actually turns recording on/off in the app (store construction with `recordAuthorship` and the `setRecordAuthorship` effect) has no test
samples.evidence: `YorkieNoteStore.setRecordAuthorship` and `NoteEditorAPI.setShowAuthors` are each covered at their own layer (yorkie-note-store.test.ts:316-346, blame-gutter.test.ts:106-166), but nothing exercises notes-view.tsx:121/166-169, which is the only place the user preference reaches the store — the privacy-relevant half of the feature. The frontend does have component-test precedent (e.g. packages/frontend/src/app/slides/toolbar/index.test.tsx), and no `*.test.tsx` exists under src/app/notes; grep for `showAuthors` in packages/frontend finds only source files, no test.

samples.summary: `sanitizeWrittenAt`'s non-numeric / non-finite / non-positive branch is untested
samples.evidence: Tests cover only the two numeric paths: a far-future `t` (yorkie-note-store.test.ts:238) and an in-skew `t` (:266). Nothing writes `t: 'abc'`, `t: -1`, `t: NaN`/`Infinity` or omits `t` while setting `a`, so the `typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite || value <= 0` guard — the guard against a forged attribute of the wrong type, which is exactly what an unvalidated CRDT attribute can be — could be deleted with the suite still green (the `at: 0` assertions for legacy text hit the `attrs === undefined` path instead).

samples.summary: MemNoteStore's `at` timestamps are never asserted, so newest-run-wins is never verified through a real store
samples.evidence: The `perChar` helper (memory.test.ts:127-134) drops `span.at` entirely, and every new memory test asserts authors only. `computeBlameLabels`' newest-wins logic is tested only against hand-built spans (blame-gutter.test.ts:56-73); in the editor tests each line is covered by a single author's run, so the end-to-end path where two authors share a line and `at` decides the label is untested with any real store. A MemNoteStore that recorded `at: 0` for every mark would pass the whole suite.

samples.summary: The equal-timestamp, document-order tiebreak (`span.at >= best.at`) is untested
samples.evidence: blame-gutter.ts:47-49 documents `>=` as a deliberate stable tiebreak for runs written in the same millisecond. No test in blame-gutter.test.ts supplies two overlapping spans with the same `at` (the 'prefers the newest run' case uses 99 vs 5), so flipping `>=` to `>` — a real behavior change for same-ms edits, which is the common case for consecutive keystrokes — breaks nothing.

verdict.reason:
I could not find any test anywhere in the repo that exercises the gutter's own sanitization at packages/notes/src/view/blame-gutter.ts:56 (`sanitizeDisplayName(best.author)`).

Verified facts:
- blame-gutter.test.ts (read in full, 193 lines) passes only 'ann'/'bob'/'cal'/''/null as span authors. The 'falls back to Anonymous when the author has no name' case (line 75-79) passes `''`, which yields ANONYMOUS_AUTHOR whether or not the sanitize call is present (`'' ?? ''` → `''` → ANONYMOUS_AUTHOR), so it is vacuous w.r.t. sanitization. The editor-level tests (lines 93-192) drive MemNoteStore with clean names only.
- No other file references computeBlameLabels / noteBlameGutter / cm-noteBlameLabel in a test: grep across packages found only blame-gutter.ts, blame-gutter.test.ts, editor.ts, index.ts, and non-test frontend UI files (notes-settings.ts, notes-toolbar.tsx, notes-view.tsx, notes-detail.tsx). There is no e2e directory.
- The nearest candidates are NOT counterexamples: yorkie-note-store.test.ts:280-297 ('strips control and bidi characters out of a claimed name', 'caps a claimed name at a displayable length') assert on `store.getAuthorSpans()[...].author`, i.e. the store's own sanitization in yorkie-note-store.ts:222 — they never touch blame-gutter.ts and would still pass if line 56 were deleted. display-name.test.ts tests the function in isolation. remote-selection.test.ts:53 covers the caret label path only (remote-selection.ts:219).
- MemNoteStore does not sanitize (memory.ts:80 setLocalAuthor stores the raw name; getAuthorSpans at ~117 passes mark.author through), so the gutter is the only sanitizing layer for that store — a gutter test with a hostile name would be trivially writable and would fail if the call were removed. Nothing like it exists.

In-lane and blocking: a new, deliberate behavior (boundary sanitization the code comment calls essential, and whose sibling caret path got its own dedicated test) ships with no test that can fail if it regresses.

finding.summary: New authorship-through-undo/redo logic in MemNoteStore (and attribution survival across Yorkie undo/redo) is untested
finding.evidence: The diff adds `authors` to MemState, snapshots it in `currentState()`/`batch()` and restores it in `restore()`. packages/notes/src/store/memory.test.ts has no occurrence of 'author' (grep returned no matches) and blame-gutter.test.ts never undoes/redoes, so removing `this.authors = state.authors.slice()` from `restore()` — leaving blame labels stale/wrong after undo — breaks no test. Likewise yorkie-note-store.test.ts's undo/redo block (lines 60+) only asserts `getText()`, never `getAuthorSpans()` after undo/redo, so attribution behaviour across Yorkie's reverse ops is entirely uncovered.

verdict.reason: The finding's core evidence is false. packages/notes/src/store/memory.test.ts contains a dedicated describe('authorship') block (lines 125-208) — 'author' appears on 10 lines, contradicting the claimed empty grep. Its test 'restores authorship on undo and redo, not just text' (L150-167) asserts per-character authorship via getAuthorSpans() after undo() ([null,null,'ann']) and after redo() ([null,null,'ann','bob']); removing `this.authors = state.authors.slice()` from restore() (memory.ts:232) would fail it. L169-183 covers the batch() authors snapshot (memory.ts:154/224) and L185-200 covers editing onto a restored authors array. The second half is likewise refuted: yorkie-note-store.test.ts:350-376 asserts getAuthorSpans() after both undo() and redo() (round-trip equality with pre-undo spans), and L378-394 asserts a peer edit stays attributed when a local change is undone. The reviewer only read the earlier undo/redo describe block near line 60 and missed the authorship block later in the same file.
